hypothesis: A serial independent last-exited oracle can separate implementation/cache defects from arithmetic and decision sensitivity on identical fixed input histories.
isolated_variables: Native attention backend: Torch versus Triton, with fixed supplied histories and dtype.
Native scheduling: serial, refill, no_refill, with the declared identical supplied histories.
BF16 versus FP32 oracle arithmetic sensitivity, diagnostic only.
Reviewed official eager fixed-depth equations versus the serial oracle, with matching supplied histories.
acceptance_criterion: Every required numerical and behavioral gate must pass for qualification; conclusive negative diagnosis remains unqualified, and incomplete or unlocalized evidence is inconclusive. Candidate dumps begin at a preselected fixture or its first observed finite required failure and stop at fixed byte limits; no earlier tensor backfill or rerun is allowed. Canonical earliest-boundary diagnosis uses preserved statistics separately from dump selection.
stop_conditions: Invalid input history or populated-cache invariant failure.
Any nonfinite value, device failure, or cleanup failure stops device work.
Per-case600s or outer7200s limit, outer limit wins.
Any declared transient, spool, disk, or dump cap exceeded; preserve missing-comparison records.
Finite tolerance failures retain planned diagnostic coverage; no replacement execution or silent source fixes.

comparison_policy.rationale: Preserve original declared FP32/BF16 logit bounds. Hidden, populated-KV and gate differences have no independently justified acceptance margins and remain diagnostic-only. Exact state/copy/lifecycle invariants are checked separately; output/token-depth overrides never count as genuine prediction agreement.
